text:
noah: quick follow-up from today's all-hands: customers asked whether we'll guarantee H100 capacity for peak holiday traffic or rely on our fallbacks. any short summary?

jamal: short: we won't buy blanket short-term racks. plan = preemptible-first burst pools + targeted reserved top-ups for explicit enterprise SLAs. non-critical traffic gets routed to smaller variants or cross-region.

rebecca: procurement ETA on extra H100s?

jamal: vendors delayed; earliest delivery slipped ~2-3 weeks. so for the holiday week we'll depend on orchestration, cross-region routing for non-residency-sensitive workloads, and reserved top-ups only where customers precommit.

noah: what happens if preemptibles fail mid-spike? ops needs the fallback steps for runbooks.

jamal: fallback flow: 1) attempt local preemptible pool; 2) after preemptible_unavail window (default 60-90s) route eligible traffic to reserved pool; 3) if reserved unavailable route to smaller model variants and mark requests degraded. we'll also cap routing to avoid overloads.

infra-bot: scheduled: burst-canary v3 at 2028-06-10T14:00:00Z by jamal.

olivia: can ops get the canary knobs to prep runbooks?

jamal: posted excerpt below for copy/paste:
```
canary_fraction: 0.1
canary_duration: 20m
preemptible_unavail_secs: 75
reserved_fallback: true
model_fallback_order: ["vbase", "vsmall"]
autoscaler_metrics: [queue_depth, gpu_util, p95_latency]
scale_up_cooldown: 20s
scale_down_cooldown: 2m
failure_inject: {preemptible_kill_pct:40, after_secs:60}
```

rebecca: good. I'll add a synthetic failure case to the canary and a cross-region latency probe. also creating INFRA-4980 for runbook updates.

noah: thanks. please loop in CS and sales so enterprise customers know how to get guaranteed capacity.

jamal: will do a short one-pager and cost estimate for a 1-week reserved top-up per region. posting to #all-hands-followups when ready.

olivia: any SDK changes required?

jamal: no client changes for default routing. server-side flags will be exposed if customers request reserved-only behavior.

noah: perfect, closing the loop.
